transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Thursday, October 8. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Veteran actor Nana Patekar passes away at 75. Nana Patekar has passed away at his residence in Goa at the age of 75. He made significant contributions to both Hindi and Marathi cinema over several decades. Patekar was known for his powerful performances and distinctive screen presence in numerous films. Throughout his career, he received multiple National Awards and a Padma Shri for his work in the arts. Some oligarchs blocking entry of Starlink in India: Elon Musk. Elon Musk has claimed that certain oligarchs are obstructing Starlink's entry into the Indian market. Starlink has already established the necessary infrastructure and is prepared to launch its services. The company aims to provide affordable broadband connectivity to areas lacking internet access. Regulatory approvals are awaited before the commercial rollout can commence in India. 'Stabbed 7 times': How bid to seal petrol pump turned deadly for IndianOil official. In a tragic incident, Mahesh Shelke, the sales manager for IndianOil, was fatally stabbed during an altercation at a petrol pump as he sought to take control of the outlet amid a dispute. Swift action was taken by authorities, resulting in the arrest of five individuals, including members of the Pandavveer family. IndianOil and the petroleum ministry have rallied to support Shelke's family during this devastating period. US to strike Iran? Pentagon orders military to gear up attacks. The Pentagon has been instructed to prepare for possible military actions against Iran, amid stalled diplomatic efforts. Preparations may lead to attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities and strategic sites, although no attack timeline has been set. This situation overlaps with renewed fighting in Yemen, where Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified. Meanwhile, elections in the US and Israel may influence military decisions in the region. Delhi Police likely to file FIR over alleged assault on police during Congress protest. Delhi Police is reviewing videos to identify protesters involved in the alleged assault during a Congress protest. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained for defying police orders while attempting to proceed to Jantar Mantar. Police are also taking action against misleading social media posts regarding their conduct during the protest. Earlier, an FIR was lodged against Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi for forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan. Google ordered to halt data center work in 'Texas of Europe; company admits 'concerns'. Google has received an order to halt construction on its data center projects in Muhos and Kajaani. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Agency has mandated that construction continues only after environmental impact assessments. Google acknowledged the concerns raised and stated that it would comply with the authority's guidance. The company has emphasized its commitment to biodiversity plans, including extensive tree planting. 'Naman Dhir has finished him': World Cup winner's big statement on star's T20I future. Naman Dhir had scored 318 runs in IPL 2026 but did not bowl a single over during the tournament. His international debut showed that he can offer India another option with the ball. Former India cricketer and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth believes Dhir's emergence could seriously hurt Washington Sundar's chances in white-ball cricket. US-based woman files case against parents for property share; Karnataka HC rejects it. The case involves a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman's father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act. The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property. IIT-B puts on hold 2026 rules on tough penalties for cheating. IIT-Bombay's senate has halted new penalties for academic misconduct, reverting to the 2015 policy for upcoming examinations. This decision follows the recent death of a student suspected of cheating during an exam. An interim procedure allows faculty to document suspected dishonesty while encouraging student accounts on a separate form. Faculty members and students will present their cases before a disciplinary committee after the examination period. Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist. As tensions escalate in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices have surged amid fears of potential supply disruptions. Recent assaults on tankers heighten the danger of transporting crude through this vital corridor. Additionally, American crude inventories are dwindling, signaling a tighter market, while diesel and jet fuel stocks remain below average levels, a trend seen for over seven months since the onset of regional conflict.

transcript.title: Bhopal and Madhya Pradesh
transcript.text: Now, news closer to home in Bhopal and across Madhya Pradesh. MP Government Promotions GAD Directs Departments To Hold DPCs For 2027 Vacancies. The Madhya Pradesh General Administration Department has directed departments to hold Departmental Promotion Committee meetings for expected 2027 vacancies under the Public Service Promotion Rules, 2025. Some MP Private Hospitals To Stop Ayushman Treatment From October 8 Over NABH Rule. Some private hospitals in Madhya Pradesh will indefinitely stop treating Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries from October 8 in protest against mandatory NABH certification, hospital associations said. SVAMITVA Row Escalates In MP, Nine Probationary Patwaris Terminated And Around 250 Get Notices. A confrontation between the Madhya Pradesh government and patwaris over the SVAMITVA scheme has intensified after nine probationary patwaris were terminated and around 250 were served notices, according to the Patwari Association. CM Mohan Yadav Inaugurates MP Travel Mart 2026, rupees 848 Crore Tourism Deal Inked. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav inaugurated the seventh Madhya Pradesh Travel Mart in Bhopal, where a rupees 848.40 crore agreement was inked for a major tourism project at Ramgarh in Sehore. Three Jain Idols Stolen From Indore Temple Found Buried In Dhar, One Arrested. Police recovered three stolen Ashtadhatu idols of Lord Mahavir, Adinath and Arahnath from Dhar district and arrested one suspect in connection with the September 16 theft from a Jain temple in Indore's Mangliya. Two cheetahs released into tiger reserve, their third habitat in Madhya Pradesh. Simultaneous heatwaves and dry spells amplify vegetation stress across Madhya Pradesh. Relationship dispute ends in gunfire: Homeopathy student shoots batchmate, attempts suicide twice in Madh. MP's Ujjain Plans Safer, Inclusive Public Spaces For Young Children And Caregivers. Ujjain Municipal Corporation held a capacity-building workshop under Nurturing Neighbourhoods 2.0 to improve public spaces for children aged up to six and their caregivers. Bhopal observes another 'No UPI Day': Rice and pulse traders stage symbolic protest against MDR charges. Azad Samaj Party Workers Block Road Outside SP Office Over College Clash In MP's Ujjain. Azad Samaj Party workers blocked the road outside the SP office in Ujjain, protesting the alleged failure to register an FIR over a clash at Government Madhav Science College. Rain in Jabalpur, Rewa-Shahdol divisions today: Alert in 12 MP districts; rain tomorrow too; sunny in Bhopa. Trees cut, funds lie unused: NGT pulls up BMC over Bhopal's green cover loss. Garbage Piles Up In Indore As Sanitation Strike Enters Day 3, BJP-Congress Trade Charges. Indore's sanitation crisis deepened as workers' strike entered its third day, disrupting garbage collection and street sweeping across several areas. MP swings into luxury tourism with 404cr golf resort near Bhopal. Shawshank redux: 'Mr Good' breaks out of jail, 8 days before parole, 9 months before freedom.

This CAS statement at present shows your demat and non-demat holdings including mutual funds, bonds, listed shares.

While much of the automotive world sits dumbfounded as China gobbles up all its customers, BMW continues to roll out extremely well-crafted, technologically advanced electric vehicles that impress in both drive quality and price. The latest is the BMW iX4, a coupe-shaped SUV that puts a sportier spin on the automaker's iX3. The iX4 is Robot data startup Mecka AI nabs $60M from Sequoia. Mecka AI collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots. The startup pays people to record everyday tasks. NASA's Webb finds signs of Mars-sized worlds smashing together. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of the kinds of violent collisions that may have shaped our own solar system, including the giant impact thought to have created the Moon. By studying 21 rare "extreme debris disks" around young stars, researchers found that their dust can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions. Apple to hold event on October 13? New Smart Home Hub, HomePod Mini and Apple TV expected. Apple is expected to announce another batch of products in the final week of October, shortly after a reported smart home product launch around October 13. Teenage Engineering's CEO says it'll stop making synths. Teenage Engineering founder and CEO Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety that it plans to stop making synths. And yes, that includes the iconic OP-1, which put the company on the map. TE isn't just a music gear maker; it's also a sought-after design firm. It's collaborated with Ikea, Nothing, and Playdate, among others. While VCs crowd into San Francisco, Endeavor Catalyst raises $320M for founders 'elsewhere'. Endeavor Catalyst just raised $320 million to keep backing founders outside Silicon Valley. Half the profits go back to the nonprofit that finds them. Taking antibiotics? Sugar may be making the damage worse. Eating more sugar while taking antibiotics was linked to greater disruption of the gut microbiome and increased growth of potentially harmful bacteria. Researchers say temporarily cutting back on sweets during and after antibiotic treatment could be a simple way to reduce this damage, though clinical trials are still needed. After Samsung, Google hikes Pixel 10a price; Here's how much it costs now in India. Google Pixel 10a was launched earlier this year at a price of rupees 49,999 in India. The phone has now recorded an increase in price of about rupees 6,000. Android's physical navigation buttons are back on Googlebooks, but not the way you think. A common misconception I've seen with Googlebooks is that the Quick Insert and Google logo keys are new. They're not, as they first debuted a couple of years ago on some Chromebooks. But there is something new for Googlebooks that's ripped straight from Android phones circa 2014. On every Googlebook keyboard, the F1, F2, and Nous Research confirms it hit $1.5B valuation, launches AI agents for business users. The developer of Hermes Agent raised a $90 million Series B. Scientists changed how zoo lions eat. Their wild side came out. Giving zoo lions whole carcasses on a feast-and-fast schedule appears to bring out more natural behavior. The lions spent nearly three times longer feeding, engaged in more tearing and manipulating of food, and rested more heavily after meals. Their activity then increased gradually during the fasting period, closely resembling the rhythm seen in wild lions. 5 gaming smartphones under rupees 50,000: Best phones for BGMI, COD Mobile and more. Looking for a gaming smartphone under rupees 50,000? Here are five options for BGMI, COD Mobile and Genshin Impact, featuring powerful processors, high-refresh-rate AMOLED displays, large batteries, fast charging and gaming-focused hardware. We found some great October Prime Day deals under $50. Getting in on the Prime Day action doesn't have to result in an empty wallet. Just as we found a couple handfuls of goodies that are under $25, there are plenty of deals during Amazon's October sale that are $50 or less, many of which offer a lot of practical value. Everything from chargers to Microsoft releases new Nvidia-chip AI PCs with revamped Windows 11. Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its Surface Laptop Ultra, AI PCs that run on Nvidia chips that are designed to run AI models and agents. Scientists reprogram immune cells inside the body to fight cancer. Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a way to create cancer-fighting CAR-T cells directly inside the body, potentially avoiding the slow and extremely expensive process of removing, engineering, and reinfusing a patient's immune cells. Using a two-particle delivery system, the researchers sent CRISPR gene-editing tools and new cancer-targeting DNA specifically into T cells, where the DNA was inserted at a precise location in the genome. Can you play GTA 6 on PC this November? Xbox clarifies cloud streaming plans ahead of launch. Xbox has denied a report claiming GTA 6 will be available to PC players through Xbox Cloud Gaming at launch on 19 November. The original report said Microsoft had secured exclusive streaming rights for the game, potentially giving PC users access to the game without an Xbox console. Roku's OLED TVs are up to $400 off during Prime Day, starting at $700. Just over a week ago, we covered a deal at Amazon that knocked around 30 percent off Roku's new (and first-ever) OLED TVs. The deal expired, but has returned for the final day of October Prime Day. The 55-inch Pro Series OLED is $699.99 at Amazon, which is 30 percent off its list price. The Meta's Muse launches on iPad just a month after its mobile debut. Meta's AI agent Muse is now available on iPad, just a month after its mobile debut, as the company rapidly expands the assistant's reach and integrations. Humans may not be as hardwired for violence as we thought. A study comparing 100 primate species, including humans, suggests that everyday aggression and lethal violence did not evolve as part of the same simple behavioral spectrum. Species that frequently fight or show mild aggression are not necessarily more likely to kill rivals, while extreme acts such as infanticide and lethal attacks appear to follow their own evolutionary patterns. Smart glasses privacy concerns grow: Norway, Australia, UK and US curb Meta Ray-Ban use. Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses are raising privacy concerns because they make it easier to capture photos, videos and audio without others knowing. Norway, Australia, the UK and the US are considering or enforcing restrictions on camera-equipped smart glasses in public and sensitive spaces.

transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. Rupee may be undervalued, markets can be irrational: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated that the rupee is undervalued and the central bank will intervene. The rupee closed at 96.78, down 36 paise from the previous day, hitting a five-month low. Malhotra mentioned that global AI stock corrections could attract foreign capital to India. Despite a robust services trade surplus, the current account deficit has widened due to increased merchandise trade deficit. Supreme Court to study plea for recall of split verdict on EC appointment law. The Supreme Court has agreed to examine a plea concerning a recent split verdict related to a 2023 election law. This law alters the appointment process for the Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners. The split verdict occurred between Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma on whether to refer the matter to a larger Constitution bench. Congress protest: Delhi Police to scan videos to identify protesters accused of assaulting personnel; FIR likely. Delhi Police is reviewing videos to identify protesters involved in the alleged assault during a Congress protest. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi were detained for defying police orders while attempting to proceed to Jantar Mantar. Police are also taking action against misleading social media posts regarding their conduct during the protest. Earlier, an FIR was lodged against Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi for forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan. 25 years in governance: President, world leaders, allies hail PM Modi. PM Narendra Modi received congratulations from leaders including President Droupadi Murmu for his 25 years in government. Home Minister Amit Shah highlighted Modi's commitment to the welfare of the poor and women's empowerment. Various international leaders expressed admiration for Modi's leadership and vision for development. Bhutan's Prime Minister likened Modi to an enlightened ruler while acknowledging his influence on Indian self-belief. Targeting of sailors must end, says government. India has condemned recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, which have injured Indian seafarers. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) emphasized the need for immediate cessation of violence. Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar mentioned ongoing communication with Russia and Ukraine regarding safe shipping proposals. Stark 73 percent decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations since 1970, India presents ground for hope: WWF Living Planet Report. A global decline of 73 percent in monitored wildlife populations occurred between 1970 and 2022. India has successfully improved populations of tigers, one-horned rhinos, and Ganga river dolphins. The report highlights threats like habitat loss, climate change, and pollution affecting wildlife. Despite the negative trends, about half of monitored populations are stable or increasing globally. 'Cash-for transfers' WhatsApp chats part of CBI dossier on Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann OSD. A set of WhatsApp chats has emerged, alleging monetary transactions involving senior Punjab government officials and DSPs. CBI's dossier includes these chats as they prepare to interrogate CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman. Allegations suggest that intermediaries received bribes for influencing transfers and policy formulations affecting IAS and IPS officers. Additionally, documents indicate potential irregularities in real estate projects and the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority. Anti-CEC protests: Opposition, police face off again; Rahul Gandhi says won't stop till Gyanesh quits. Opposition members from the INDIA bloc attempted to stage a protest demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. They were detained by Delhi Police less than a kilometer from their protest site at Jantar Mantar. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge organized the lunch gathering, where the protest plan was discussed. Difficulties in moving their buses led to further confrontations with police as they sought to demonstrate. 'We'll do it': PM Modi gives slogan for 2047 goals; credits people's support for 25-year unbroken run. PM Narendra Modi delivered a speech highlighting his 25 years in government and the goal of developed India by 2047. He called upon citizens to commit to this ambitious target and emphasized the power of the people. Modi reiterated the importance of extraordinary goals, linking good governance to societal inclusion. He reflected on his journey from humble beginnings to leadership in the BJP. Grenade seizure case: Pakistan-based ultra declared 'proclaimed offender'. A special NIA court in Jammu has declared Nazir Hussain a proclaimed offender regarding grenade seizures. Hussain, originally from Hari village, is believed to be hiding in Pakistan currently. The court noted that previous non-bailable arrest warrants could not be executed due to his absence from home. Additionally, multiple attempts to compel Hussain to surrender have been unsuccessful. India's first high-altitude snow leopard safari flagged off in Ladakh. Ladakh has commenced India's first high-altitude wildlife safari that highlights snow leopard trails and community involvement. Vinai Kumar Saxena, the lieutenant governor, emphasized the importance of coexisting wildlife and development. The Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation Society is coordinating this project with local forest departments. The mapped safari routes traverse significant wildlife areas, including Hemis National Park and Changthang. NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist Shabir Shah in 1996 funeral violence case. A Jammu NIA court rejected the bail application of Shabir Ahmad Shah, linked to a 30-year-old mob violence case. This case relates to violence during a terrorist's funeral procession in Srinagar, which Shah allegedly incited. The court expressed concern about potential threats to national security and the safety of protected witnesses. Shah argued that the investigation was reopened without justification and emphasized delays in legal actions. Rashtriya Indian Military College Entrance Exam 2026: Correction Window Opens October 9. Additional fees may apply if corrections alter the exam fee. Israel Strikes Gaza On October 7 Anniversary, 5 Dead: Officials. In Gaza City, Al INDIA Bloc Protest Live Updates: Mamata Banerjee To Join Opposition Protest In Delhi Today. INDIA Bloc Protest Live News Updates

transcript.title: Around the world
transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests. The step comes after several groups complained of police using disproportionate force towards teenagers. Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness. People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely. Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia. Fears that the death may have been caused by pneumonic plague has prompted calls for more transparency from Russia. Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations. The 73-year-old has been arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations. Chinese runner dropped by sponsor after riding bike during marathon. Sun Yuanyuan was seemingly pictured on the back of another person's bike during part of the Berlin Marathon. Ten people linked to Kenya's first-ever Ebola case quarantined as screening concerns grow. The patient passed through multiple cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and eventually flew to Kenya. What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?. The death of a worker from a Russian lab that researches plague has prompted questions about the disease. What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and how did she survive?. The convicted killer of Colleen Slemmer is said to be awake and speaking in hospital in Tennessee after an execution attempt. Many Nepalis swept away in the floods aren't officially dead, leaving families in limbo. Relatives are finding themselves with no compensation and facing an administrative nightmare. The Republican candidates walking a Trump tightrope. Some running in November's elections are deciding whether to distance themselves from an unpopular president who still dominates his party. Drinking and consent - Cornell rape allegations expose 'loopholes' in laws. The BBC speaks to experts about current US state sexual assault laws and why some believe changing them will help alleged victims. What we know about Christa Pike's 'unprecedented' recovery after failed execution. The BBC's Sarah Smith details the injuries sustained by the US death row inmate after two failed lethal injections, and what comes next. Watch: Riot police clash with school protesters and use tear gas in France. Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France amid a wave of protests by high-school pupils. Why is Guantanamo prison still open?. Guantanamo Bay opened after the US invasion of Afghanistan. 25 years later, the war is over, but the prison remains open
